messages:
Mira (Customer): Hey team — customers on AcmeCorp private deployment (on-prem ingress behind corporate gateway) are seeing SSE streams drop after ~18-22s. Client reconnects but often gets partial text or a 401 on resume. Routing same client through our VPC endpoint works fine.

Ava (Support): ugh, thanks for reporting. Can you paste minimal repro steps and any curl / client flags you used? Also, do you see any proxy logs? :eyes:

Mira (Customer): repro: on a laptop inside corp network run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N \
  "https://private.acme.acme-corp/v1/streams?model=gpt-4r"
```
Behavior: SSE events start streaming fine, then connection goes FIN/RST from corporate gateway after ~20s. Client retries (exponential backoff) but when reconnecting sometimes get a 401 even though token is valid. If I run same curl from home (no corp proxy) stream stays up for minutes.

Mira (Customer): Proxy logs show: `X-Proxy-Action: inspect|buffer` and a line like `tcp_conn reset due to content-length mismatch`. Attached tcpdump snippet (trimmed):
```
15:03:21.123 IP client > proxy: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 0, win 64240, options [mss 1360,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0], length 0
15:03:21.124 IP proxy > server: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 321 ecr 123], length 0
```

Mira (Customer): note MSS on client side 1360, server side 1460. Also observe chunk boundary splitting at ~1500 bytes in our SSE frames.

Diego (SRE): looks like MSS clamping by corporate gateway and asymmetric MSS negotiation -> PMTU issues. If proxy is doing TLS inspection / re-write it might buffer and tear down long-lived chunked connections. Can you confirm if the corp proxy is doing SSL/TLS inspection (MITM)?

Mira (Customer): yes their appliance does TLS inspection + content scanning (they mentioned 'prevent data exfil').

Dan (Eng Runtime): important detail: our runtime sends SSE frames as chunked chunks that can be > 1500 bytes if responses include long tokens before we flush. Some enterprise proxies aggressively buffer until a full TLS record or until they hit a threshold, then reset on perceived protocol error. Two immediate mitigations: 1) enable smaller chunk flushes (runtime config: `stream.flush_threshold_bytes`) to keep each chunk < 1200 bytes; 2) add application-level heartbeat comments every 5s to keep proxy from timing out.

Ava (Support): thumbs up. Quick repro suggestion for customer: run curl with keepalive and no-buffer flags to see if proxy behavior changes:
```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Connection: keep-alive" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 'https://private.../v1/streams?model=..'
```
Also ask them to test bypassing TLS inspection (if allowed) or set proxy to not buffer for `text/event-stream` endpoints.

Lina (Net Eng): confirmed pattern: MSS clamp to 1360 can cause fragmentation or cause intermediary to rewrite segments. If the proxy rewrites TLS records (MITM), it may also change record boundaries causing downstream servers to see different packetization and the proxy to drop connections when chunked encoding doesn't match its heuristic. We should advise customer to either: increase their internal MTU to match external path or configure the proxy to allow larger TCP windows / avoid buffering SSE.

Mira (Customer): also saw auth oddness: reconnect attempt gets 401 from our side. We think client reuses a short-lived session header from initial request -> when proxy resets the TCP session the reconnect hits our auth path which sometimes rejects due to nonce reuse. Any ideas?

Dan (Eng Runtime): two things: 1) ensure client sends full fresh Authorization header on each reconnect (we've seen some clients drop header on automatic reconnects), 2) on server side we return 401 when token is invalid — but we could improve resiliency by returning a 401+`WWW-Authenticate` so clients know to refresh rather than retry blindly. We'll add a note to our troubleshooting guide.

Ava (Support): billing note: customer says repeated reconnects resulted in multiple billed requests because each reconnect is a distinct streaming session. @finance FYI — we'll likely request a one-off credit if this is a platform-side cause.

Diego (SRE): next steps for us: 
- Ask customer to run `tcpdump -s 0 -w capture.pcap port 443` during repro and send pcap.
- Customer to test with `--no-buffer` and a smaller chunk size.
- Network team (Lina) to review proxy logs to confirm MSS clamping + TLS inspection behavior.
- Runtime (Dan) to add quick fai-safe: lower default flush threshold on dedicated/private bundles to 1200 bytes for next patch.

Lina (Net Eng): I'll reach out to AcmeCorp's network admin and ask them to check proxy config — specifically any `max-record-size`, `mss-clamp`, or `buffering` rules for long-lived connections. If they can't change it we can document the workaround (heartbeat + smaller frames).

Ava (Support): created ticket Redwood-9876 and assigned: @Lina (network), @Dan (runtime), @Diego (SRE). Mira, can you attach the pcap & proxy config snippet to the ticket? We'll treat as high priority. :white_check_mark:

Mira (Customer): attaching pcap now. One more note — dedicated capacity (reserved GPU) streams behave the same when routed through corp gateway. VPC-hosted endpoints are fine. Seems strictly proxy/path dependent.

ops-bot: Incident note: support ticket Redwood-9876 opened by Ava (Support) at 2026-07-15T15:10:00Z.

Ava (Support): thanks all. We'll follow up in the ticket with a recommended runtime patch and a network config template for customers to present to their proxy vendor. Closing loop once we confirm fix or customer config change. :pray:
